payload.name: Preserve Prior Facts on Memory Update
payload.description: When updating an existing memory about a project or activity, if the new message adds details or mentions a related topic without explicitly contradicting the stored facts, preserve the original facts instead of overwriting them.
content: During UPDATE on an existing memory, first compare the new message's claims with the memory's current explicit facts.

If the new message only adds detail, reframes the topic, or mentions a related project, do not replace the existing memory; instead add a new candidate or merge only the genuinely new attributes while keeping the original facts unchanged.

Only overwrite a stored fact when the new message explicitly contradicts it. When it does, preserve the old factual span by setting world_end or retaining the older version, and do not move world_start unless the message explicitly corrects the start date.
Stop after deciding the update; do not search for additional evidence or expand the memory beyond what the message states.

solves: The Construction Agent sometimes replaces a previously stored, still-valid fact (e.g., a project name or start date) when a later message describes a related but different aspect of the same activity. This destroys evidence needed for temporal queries. This skill prevents destructive overwrites by requiring an explicit contradiction before replacing facts, and by keeping old facts or creating separate memories when the new message merely adds or shifts topic.
